body:
Found reviewing #863.

Since culturebotai-claw#571, the unified builder publishes MIM's label-index answer ahead of a recipe's own `term.id`. Where MIM's ruling is wrong, the snapshot is now wrong in the same way. The reviewer rebuilt main's MIM inputs with the same claw (a5d56296) and CultureMech (0e409dd9): that build differs from #863's snapshot only in the rows #863 changes on purpose. So every rebuild with the pinned producer publishes these rows. Their causes are in MIM records.

For most of these rows `culturemech_term_id` is now blank as well. claw's `_published_ids` withholds a same-prefix recipe id that disagrees with MIM, so the recipe's own id no longer appears anywhere in the row.

Values below are from the snapshot #863 publishes. Labels were checked against the local ChEBI build.

**Right on main, wrong now**

| Labels (occurrences) | main `chebi_id` | now `chebi_id` / `mim_id` | Source record | Fix tracked in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MgSO .7H O` (17) | CHEBI:31795 | CHEBI:32599 / CHEBI:32599 | `Magnesium_Sulfate.yaml` (synonym on the anhydrous record) | #811 |
| `DL-Na-malate` (3), `DL-Sodium malate` (2), `Na malate` (4), `Na-DL-malate` (4), `Na-malate` (6), `Na2-DL-malate` (6), `Sodium DL-malate` (11), `Sodium malate` (14) | CHEBI:91260 | CHEBI:91261 / CHEBI:91261 | `Sodium_Malate.yaml` ((S)-malate identity, DL synonyms) | #811 |
| `Na2SiO3` (8) | CHEBI:60720 | CHEBI:132108 / CHEBI:132108 | `Na2sio3_X_9_H2o.yaml` (anhydrous name on the nonahydrate) | #811 |
| `Magnesium Chloride` (5) | CHEBI:6636 | CHEBI:86345 / CHEBI:86345 | `Magnesium_Chloride.yaml` (identity is the hexahydrate) | #811 |
| `DL-Tryptophan` (4) | CHEBI:27897 | CHEBI:57912 / CHEBI:57912 | `Dl-tryptophan.yaml` (identity is L-tryptophan zwitterion) | #811 |
| `H3BO2` (3) | CHEBI:33118 | CHEBI:38267 / CHEBI:38267 | `H3bo2.yaml` (boronic acid; label likely means boric acid) | #811 |

**Wrong on main, wrong differently now**

| Labels (occurrences) | main `chebi_id` | now `chebi_id` / `mim_id` | Source record | Fix tracked in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MgSO4 x H2O` (6), `MgSO4 . H2O` (1) | CHEBI:32599 | CHEBI:31795 / CHEBI:31795 | REJECTED tombstone `Mgso47h2o.yaml` | #811 |
| `NiCl2 x H2O` (3), `NiCl2・H2O` (1) | CHEBI:34887 | CHEBI:53542 / CHEBI:53542 | tombstone `Nicl2_X_6_H2o.yaml` | #811 |
| `NaH2PO4 x H2O` (22), `NaH2PO4・H2O` (1), `NaH2PO4·H2O` (1) | CHEBI:37585 | (none) / kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o | `Nah2po4_X_2_H2o.yaml` (monohydrate spellings on the dihydrate) | #758 |
| `Potassium phosphate` (2) | CHEBI:131527 | CHEBI:63036 / CHEBI:63036 | `Kh2po4.yaml` | #811 |
| `MnSO4・xH2O` (61) | CHEBI:86360 | CHEBI:86364 / CHEBI:86364 | tombstone `Mnso4_X_1_H2o.yaml` (variable hydrate pinned to the monohydrate) | #811 |

**Generic class whose row CAS names a specific compound (untracked before this issue)**

| Labels (occurrences) | main `chebi_id` | now `chebi_id` / `mim_id` | Source record | Fix tracked in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MES` (80) | CHEBI:39005 | CHEBI:39010 / CHEBI:39010 | `Mes.yaml`: identity CHEBI:39010 (structureless class), CAS 4432-31-9 is the free acid CHEBI:39005 | this issue |
| `Inositol` (24) | CHEBI:17268 | CHEBI:24848 / CHEBI:24848 | `Inositol.yaml`: identity CHEBI:24848 inositol, CAS 87-89-8 is myo-inositol CHEBI:17268 | this issue |
| `Vitamin B12` (2155), `vitamin B12` (27) | (none) | CHEBI:176843 / CHEBI:176843 | `Vitamin_B12.yaml`: identity CHEBI:176843 (vitamer class), CAS 68-19-9 is cyanocobalamin | this issue |

**What to do**
- **#811 and #758 rows:** fix the source records listed in the table, retyping wrong-form synonyms to `REJECTED_LABEL` or correcting the identity, then rebuild the snapshot. The rejection ledger cannot fix these rows, because it cannot reject MIM's own identity.
- **The three class rows (MES, Inositol, Vitamin B12):** decide whether each record denotes the specific compound its CAS names (MES free acid CHEBI:39005, myo-inositol CHEBI:17268, cyanocobalamin), or whether the CAS should be withdrawn from a class-level identity. Vitamin B12 alone accounts for 2,182 recipe occurrences.

Publishing these rows in #863 was an explicit decision. The #863 review counted 27 rows (3,227 occurrences) that the same rebuild moves from an anhydrous term to the correct hydrate term. It also stops 20 hydrate rows (241 occurrences) from publishing their anhydrous parent, relative to main.
title: Unified mapping now publishes MIM's wrong label-index identities for 26 labels (claw#571 rebuild in #863)

body:
Independent adversarial review of the approved #914 replacement found raw CultureMech term IDs promoting labels with no MIM name owner into unrelated or insufficiently scoped MIM identities.

Confirmed cases:
- `MnSO4·xH2O` becomes anhydrous CHEBI:86360/CAS7785-87-7 (17 occurrences), despite existing MIM rejection of variable-hydrate aliases. Source: CultureMech `bacterial/JCM_J1503_AUTOTROPHIC_NITROBACTER_MEDIUM.yaml`; [ChEBI86360](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:86360) denotes the anhydrous salt.
- `Cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12)` becomes generic class CHEBI:176843 through `algae/yt75s_v.yaml`, despite the MIM class record explicitly rejecting the cyanocobalamin member name. [ChEBI176843](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:176843) is the class.

Ten additional preparation-qualified labels have no MIM name anchor and acquire pure-compound identity through the same fallback:
- `1 M K2HPO4` → `CHEBI:131527`
- `1 M KH2PO4` → `CHEBI:63036`
- `1 M Sodium acetate solution` → `CHEBI:32954`
- `1 M Tris base (pH 8)` → `CHEBI:9754`
- `1 N NaOH` → `CHEBI:32145`
- `10% Glucose solution` → `CHEBI:17234`
- `25% HCl (7.7 M)` → `CHEBI:17883`
- `5% L-Cysteine·HCl·H2O solution` → `CHEBI:91248`
- `5% Na2S·9H2O solution` → `CHEBI:76209`
- `8% NaHCO3 solution` → `CHEBI:32139`

Under MAPPING_SEMANTICS §0 these need explicit preparation-scope review, not inferred exact identity. The safe export repair rejects the named raw source ID for that exact label without inventing a replacement or minting a record. The existing four-column rejection ledger currently cannot express a rejection without an asserted replacement MIM ID; its supported contract must be extended narrowly in the producer and local gate. Keep source names/counts, scope rejections by label+ID, preserve a valid explicit MIM name owner, and do not globally blacklist an ontology term. Regenerate with zero unsafe identities on these held pairs, add regressions, rerun native QC and independent review.

This is a dependency of the approved #914 redo, separate from step5 SSSOM owned-name policy. Existing related source/label issues #811 and #868 remain distinct. Evidence: `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step1-independent/unified-fallback-findings.json` and `unified-54-identity-owner-check.json`; diagnostic snapshot SHA256 `e5c4bd6b5512606857feded03a45591476ce64626c261315f7ed2bed1f742f8a`. No scientific approval is granted by withholding.
title: Hold unsupported raw-source identity promotions in the refreshed unified snapshot

body:
Found while adding synonym matching to CultureMech's divergence audit against
your published SSSOM (CultureBotAI/CultureMech#304).

## The defect

In `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`, the row

```
subject_label : CaSO4 x 2 H2O
object_id     : CHEBI:32583  (calcium sulfate dihydrate)
```

carries **potassium phosphate aliases** in its `other` column:

```
other: (dibasic)|CaSO4|CaSO4 . 2H2O|CaSO4 x 2H2O|...|KH PO|KH2PO4|...|Potassium dihydrogen phosphate|...
```

`KH2PO4`, `KH PO` and `Potassium dihydrogen phosphate` are not aliases of calcium
sulfate dihydrate. They belong to the neighbouring `KH2PO4 → CHEBI:63036` row,
which is present and correct.

## Why it matters downstream

`Potassium dihydrogen phosphate` appears in the `other` column of **this row and
no other**, so a consumer that indexes aliases sees it as an unambiguous mapping
to `CHEBI:32583`. In CultureMech that would have told **233 ingredient rows** they
should be calcium sulfate dihydrate.

An ambiguity check does not help: a bad alias that occurs exactly once looks
exactly like a good one. We caught it only by eyeballing the newly-surfaced
disagreements before trusting them, and consequently left alias matching opt-in
rather than promoting it to our gate.

## Suggested fix

Remove the potassium-phosphate tokens from the `CaSO4 x 2 H2O` row's `other`.

Worth a sweep for the same shape, since whatever produced it may have merged
other adjacent rows: an alias whose element set is disjoint from its row's own
label is a cheap detector — `KH2PO4` shares no element with `CaSO4 x 2 H2O`
beyond O. CultureMech's `scripts/audit_name_term_elements.py` does the equivalent
check for groundings and could be adapted.

## Notes

- No action needed on CultureMech's side; we simply do not consume aliases by
  default.
- Happy to send the sweep results if that is useful.
title: CaSO4 x 2 H2O row carries KH2PO4 aliases, so consumers map potassium phosphate to calcium sulfate
